findings.where: slides/02.png (map and caption), script-3min-en.md demo line B1 and beat 5, video-30s.md 0:10-0:20
findings.problem: The deck says the planner blocks cells over 20 degrees and the demo says the route 'never crosses slopes over twenty degrees'. The map on slide 2 shows stop 1 (WP3, Bright Angel) drawn inside the red band, with the route line running to it. code-facts.md confirms it: WP3 sits on a 28.7 degree slope, the planner stops up to 20 m short, and arrival still needs the walker within 2 m of the point. So the 913 m scenario route to Cheyava Falls passes a stop the astronaut can only reach by stepping on no-go ground. A judge who reads the legend sees the contradiction on the slide itself.
findings.proposal: Move the WP3 marker to the nearest cell under 20 degrees, or widen its arrival radius to the planner's stand-off (20 m), then re-export the slide 2 map. If there is no time, drop WP3 from the slide 2 route (plan HAB to Cheyava Falls only) and re-check that 913 m, 54 g and 18 min still hold. Keep 'never crosses' only if the picture agrees.

findings.where: slides/03.png (oxygen bar and visor screenshot), slides/04.png (Walk +480, React +399), script beat 5
findings.problem: The hero number does not survive arithmetic done on the slide. 72 g for 30 min is 2.4 g/min, so 34 g is 14 minutes, not 13. The slide never says which rate turns grams into minutes. code-facts.md shows why: the margin divides O2 left by the current smoothed rate (suitModel.js:244-251), so it reads +399 or +480 min with the same 100 % tank depending on whether she is standing or walking. An EVA flight controller would ask whether resting inflates the margin. It does.
findings.proposal: Add one line under the bar on slide 3 with the rate behind the 13 min (for example '34 g at her rate on the alert frame, 2.6 g/min'), or recompute the green slice at the same walking rate as the reserve and show 14 min everywhere. Add a Q&A answer that says the margin uses the current 30 s smoothed rate and that a planning rate is the next fix.

findings.where: slides/03.png headline 'Marswalk says: head home now', script beat 5 'Marswalk sends her home now', beats.md beat 3
findings.problem: The Cheyava Falls answer comes from an offline script (docs/pitch/tools/walkback-zone.mjs), not from a state a judge can reach in the app. The demo shows a 55 m sortie with a dust storm fired by hand, and the visor screenshot on slide 3 shows +399 min, not 13. Starting a Cheyava Falls EVA at 20 % O2 at the habitat is no-go, so nobody can reproduce '13 minutes' by scanning the QR. The captions are honest in small type, but the headline credits the app.
findings.proposal: Say it once in plain words on slide 3 and in beat 5: 'computed with the app's planner and suit model for this scenario'. Better, put the alert-frame numbers (position, O2 left, walk-home grams, margin) from walkback-zone.json in the repo README with the command that produces them, and name that file on slide 3 so a judge can check it.

findings.problem: Slide 5 promises 'what each decides', and three rows say more than the build does. Row 1 lists 'its 25 cm image' but the app ships the orthomosaic at 3000 px over 1422 m, about 0.5 m per pixel. Row 3, MEDA, shows a replayed outlook next to go / no-go and the HUD temperature and wind; code-facts.md shows no path from MEDA into the route, the cost or the decision. Row 4, RAD, is a stepped table of two dose rates in radiation.json; the rad.json event curve is never read (medaRad.js:182 has no caller) and the event background is 10 uGy/h against 8.75 on the HUD. HiRISE is core and that part is strong. The other sources are parameters and displays.
findings.proposal: Row 1: '25 cm image, shown at 0.5 m'. Row 3: 'Temperature, pressure and wind shown before go / no-go and on the visor'. Row 4: 'Background and peak dose rate of the radiation alert; the storm's opacity, above 8.0'. Change the kicker to 'Five NASA sources, what each one feeds'. Giving HiRISE the weight and the rest one honest line each scores better with a data judge than five equal rows.

findings.where: script cold open and beat 5, qa.md question 5, slides/04.png React banner
findings.problem: The jeopardy in the cold open is a radiation alert, and the event behind it peaks at 29.92 uGy/h, three times background. The whole 2017 event added 544 uGy, about two and a half sols of normal dose. A radiation or EVA judge will ask why that aborts a biosignature sampling stop. The Q&A answers 'why Gale' and not 'why abort for this dose'.
findings.proposal: Add a Q&A answer: the alert is an early warning, nobody knows the size of an event when the flare is seen, so the rule is shelter early (ALARA); September 2017 is the only solar particle event measured from the ground on Mars, and it was mild, 544 uGy in total. Put 'early warning' in the spoken beat 5 so the abort reads as procedure, not as a lethal dose.

findings.where: video-30s.md 0:20-0:30 narration, slides/07.png, slides/05.png row 4, qa.md question 6
findings.problem: Two wording slips. The video says 'We process the same HiRISE model as NASA Mars Trek, to fourteen centimetres', which a listener hears as terrain accuracy. It is a resampling check against the same product, and the deck says so correctly. The storm opacity is given as 'peak opacity 8.0' while the source in hazards.json reads 'above 8.0', a lower bound.
findings.proposal: Video: 'Our grid reproduces NASA's HiRISE model to fourteen centimetres.' Slide 5 and Q&A 6: 'above 8.0'. If Q&A time allows, name what the 0.14 m does not cover, the DTM's own vertical error.

advance.why: HiRISE is the working core of the product. The DTM sets slope, the no-go mask, the A* cost, the oxygen per leg and the radio shadow, and the team checked its grid against the served product at 564,001 nodes. The walkback margin is a real EVA planning rule with Apollo 15 and 17 sources, and the measured / derived / assumed tags, the 'Gale, not Jezero' line and the lunar-suit caveat are more candid than most entries. The 3-minute script, the 7 slides and the video make none of the listed false claims; the six slips sit in the 5-minute table and the Q&A sheet. I would send it forward, with the marks held down on Validity until the slide 2 route and the 13-minute arithmetic are fixed.
advance.change_my_mind: I would vote no if the scenario route really requires walking on ground over 20 degrees and the pitch still says 'never crosses', if the 13 minutes cannot be reproduced from a file in the repo, or if a presenter says '1 m terrain', '16 cm against the rover' or 'real 2017 doses' out loud from the Q&A sheet.
